title: Individual software project with unrestricted LLM use except unit tests
summary: Students independently conceptualize, design, implement, test, and document a Python application over seven weekly iterations. LLM use is unrestricted for code and documentation, but students must write unit tests themselves and report how they used AI.

sources.title: Unrestricted Use of LLMs in a Software Project Course: Student Perceptions on Learning and Impact on Course Performance
sources.evidence_quote: Course participants are allowed to freely use LLMs, except that AI-generated unit tests are not allowed.

context.learner_level: primarily second-year undergraduate computer science students

assessment.summary: Build an open-ended Python application with a user interface and persistent data, following a seven-week software-development process.
student_actions: Conceptualize, design, implement, test, and document an application.
Advance the project through weekly goals.
Create unit and integration tests without AI generation.
Report LLM use for code and documentation.

student_role.description: LLMs may be used freely except to generate unit tests.

grading.method: Teaching-assistant assessment of code, documentation, tests, peer review, weekly goals, and required exercises.

criteria.description: User interface, storage, logic, scope, library use, release, code quality, and error management.

process: A minimum of 28 of 61 points is required to pass.
Maximum testing points require at least 70% unit-test branch coverage plus appropriate unit and integration testing.

reported_results: 80.5% of spring 2024 respondents reported using an LLM.
LLM use patterns were compared with total project points and time spent.
